rules.title: PowerShell 7.3 is no longer supported
rules.summary: Microsoft's PowerShell support lifecycle lists 7.3 (built on .NET 7.0) as retired: support ended on 2024-05-08, so it receives no further updates, including security updates. A script or manifest that requires 7.3 targets an unsupported release.

rules.title: PowerShell 7.2 (LTS) is no longer supported
rules.summary: Microsoft's PowerShell support lifecycle lists 7.2 LTS (built on .NET 6.0) as retired: support ended on 2024-11-08, so it receives no further updates, including security updates. A script or manifest that requires 7.2 targets an unsupported release.

rules.title: PowerShell 7.1 is no longer supported
rules.summary: Microsoft's PowerShell support lifecycle lists 7.1 (built on .NET 5.0) as retired: support ended on 2022-05-08, so it receives no further updates, including security updates. A script or manifest that requires 7.1 targets an unsupported release.

rules.title: PowerShell 7.0 (LTS) is no longer supported
rules.summary: Microsoft's PowerShell support lifecycle lists 7.0 LTS (built on .NET Core 3.1) as retired: support ended on 2022-12-03, so it receives no further updates, including security updates. A script or manifest that requires 7.0 targets an unsupported release.

rules.title: PowerShell 6.x is no longer supported
rules.summary: Microsoft's PowerShell support lifecycle lists every PowerShell 6 release (6.0, 6.1, and 6.2) as retired; the last, 6.2, reached end of support on 2020-09-04. A script or manifest that requires a 6.x version targets an unsupported release.
